sections.title: AI Services for New York Legal Organizations
sections.description: Production AI solutions for New York's world-leading legal market.

blocks.heading: Contract Intelligence and M&A Due Diligence
paragraphs: For New York's M&A practices and corporate departments — where Skadden, Wachtell, Sullivan & Cromwell, and Davis Polk handle the largest deals in the world:

Contract extraction at deal scale: NLP extracting material provisions from hundreds or thousands of contracts in M&A data rooms — change of control triggers, assignment restrictions, termination rights, indemnification obligations, and representations for deal team analysis in hours rather than weeks.

Regulatory filing intelligence: RAG over SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statements) for M&A teams conducting regulatory and antitrust due diligence at the volume that New York's largest deals generate.
Data room Q&A: RAG over entire M&A data room document sets — enabling deal team members to ask natural language questions across thousands of documents.
Cost: $55,000–$150,000 | Timeline: 12–24 weeks | Privilege-aware RBAC

blocks.heading: E-Discovery and Litigation AI
paragraphs: For New York's commercial litigation practices — where securities class actions, antitrust litigation, and complex commercial disputes generate the largest e-discovery volumes in the country:

Predictive coding (TAR): Technology-Assisted Review for document relevance review in New York's massive e-discovery workflows — reducing review costs by 60–80% while meeting SDNY and EDNY e-discovery standards.

Privilege logging automation: AI identifying potentially privileged documents and generating privilege log entries — reducing the manual review burden of privilege review in large New York litigations.
Deposition preparation: RAG over deposition transcripts, expert reports, and document productions enabling litigators to query evidence for deposition preparation.
Cost: $50,000–$140,000 | Timeline: 12–22 weeks | SDNY e-discovery standards

blocks.heading: Securities and Regulatory Intelligence
paragraphs: For New York's securities law practices and financial regulatory counsel:
SEC enforcement monitoring: AI scanning SEC enforcement actions, no-action letters, and staff guidance for pattern recognition and compliance risk assessment.
Securities disclosure review: NLP comparing draft proxy statements and registration statements against historical SEC comment patterns — predicting SEC staff comments before filing.
Regulatory change intelligence: LLM systems synthesizing SEC, FINRA, CFTC, and NYDFS rulemaking for New York securities counsel's regulatory advisory practices.
Cost: $45,000–$120,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks

sections.title: New York Legal AI Considerations
sections.description: Attorney-client privilege, NYDFS intersection, and bar compliance for NYC legal AI.

blocks.heading: Attorney-client privilege protection
paragraphs: Every New York legal AI system must be designed with attorney-client privilege as the primary data governance principle — user access controls that enforce privilege at the document and matter level, audit logging of all document access, and deployment options (self-hosted for the most sensitive matters) that prevent unauthorized disclosure.

blocks.heading: NYDFS and financial regulatory law intersection
paragraphs: New York's securities and financial regulatory practices operate within the NYDFS, FINRA, and SEC regulatory frameworks. Legal AI for New York's financial regulatory practice groups must understand this intersection — regulatory document processing for securities enforcement defense requires specific handling.

blocks.heading: Bar compliance for AI-assisted legal work
paragraphs: New York State Bar Association guidance on AI use in legal practice evolves as AI capabilities advance. ClickMasters designs legal AI as attorney assistance (supervised workflows) rather than autonomous legal advice, consistent with current NY Bar ethics guidance.

sections.title: Objections, Answered Directly
sections.description: Addressing common questions about New York legal AI development.

blocks.heading: "BigLaw has existing technology relationships — why would Sullivan & Cromwell work with ClickMasters?"
paragraphs: ClickMasters works with BigLaw's vendor ecosystem, LegalTech companies selling into BigLaw, and corporate legal departments that have different technology relationships than their outside counsel. Not every New York legal AI opportunity requires direct BigLaw engagement.

blocks.heading: "How much does legal AI cost in New York?"
paragraphs: $40,000–$150,000 for most New York legal AI applications. M&A due diligence at scale and LegalTech product AI at the higher end.

blocks.heading: "Can AI handle attorney-client privilege protection reliably?"
paragraphs: Privilege protection is a design requirement, not a model capability. ClickMasters designs with privilege-protective RBAC, access logging, and output validation — but privilege determination ultimately requires attorney judgment, not AI.

blocks.heading: "How long does legal AI development take in New York?"
paragraphs: 10–24 weeks.
